source_text: Incutiat adhuc scorpius, homicidam Deum ventilans: horrebo plane spurcum blasphemiae statum de haeretico ore foetentem; sed et talem Deum de fiducia rationis amplectar, qua ratione etiam ipse se plus quam homicidam pronuntiavit ex Sophiae suae persona, voce Salomonis: Sophia, inquit, jugulavit filios suos. Sophia, sapientia est. Sapienter utique jugulavit, dum in vitam; et rationaliter, dum in gloriam. O parricidii ingenium! o sceleris artificium! o argumentum crudelitatis, quae idcirco occidit, ne moriatur quem occiderit! Et ideo quid sequitur? Sophia in exitibus cantatur hymnis,; cantatur enim et exitus martyrum. Sophia in plateis de constantia agit, bene enim filios suos jugulat. Super summos autem muros confisa dicit, cum quidem secundum Isaiam hic exclamat: Ego Dei sum; et hic vociferatur: In nomine Jacob; et alius scribit, In nomine Israelis. O bonam matrem! Opto et ipse in filios ejus redigi, ut ab ea occidar. Opto occidi, ut filius fiam. Solum autem jugulat filios suos; an et torquet? Audio enim et alibi dicentem Deum: Uram illos sicuti uritur argentum, et probabo illos sicuti probatur aurum. Utique per tormenta ignium et suppliciorum, per martyria fidei examinatoria. Scit et Apostolus qualem Deum adscripserit, cum scribit: Si Deus Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis tradidit illum, quomodo non et cum illo omnia condonavit nobis? Vides quomodo etiam proprium suum Filium primogenitum et unigenitum Sophia divina jugulaverit; utique victurum, imo et caeteros in vitam redacturum. Possum dicere cum Sophia Dei: Christus est qui se tradidit pro delictis nostris. Jam et semetipsam Sophia trucidavit. Verba non sono solo sapiunt, sed et sensu: nec auribus tantummodo audienda sunt, sed et mentibus. Crudelem Deum, qui non intelligit, credit. Quamquam et non intelligenti posita sententia est, quae temeritatem cohibeat aliter intelligendi. Quis enim, inquit, cognovit sensum Dei? aut quis illi consiliarius fuit, qui eum instruat? aut viam intelligentiae quis demonstravit illi? Sed enim Scytharum Dianam, aut Gallorum Mercurium, aut Afrorum Saturnum, hominum victima placari apud saeculum licuit. Et Latio ad hodiernum Jovi media in urbe humanus sanguis ingustatur; nec quisquam retractat, aut non rationem praesumit aliquam, aut inaestimabilem Dei sui voluntatem. Si noster quoque Deus propriae hostiae nomine martyria sibi depostulasset, quis illi exprobrasset funestam religionem, et lugubres ritus, et aram rogum, et pollinctorem sacerdotem? et non beatum amplius reputasset, quem Deus comedisset?
pass_a_gloss: Still the scorpion stings, ventilating God as a homicide; I will shudder plainly at the foul state of blasphemy foetentem from the heretic's mouth; but I will also embrace such a God with confidence of reason, by which reason He Himself also pronounced Himself more than a homicide from the person of His Wisdom, in the voice of Solomon: Wisdom, He says, has slain her sons. Wisdom is wisdom. Certainly, she slew wisely, since into life; and rationally, since into glory. O genius of parricide! O art of crime! O argument of cruelty, which kills for this reason, that he whom it kills may not die! And therefore what follows? Wisdom is sung in exits with hymns; for exits of martyrs are also sung. Wisdom acts in the streets concerning constancy, for she slays her sons well. But on the highest walls, trusting, she says, since according to Isaiah she exclaims here: I am of God; and here she cries out: In the name of Jacob; and another writes: In the name of Israel. O good mother! I also wish to be reduced to her sons, so that I may be killed by her. I wish to be killed, so that I may become a son. Does she only slay her sons; or also torment them? For I hear God saying elsewhere: I will refine them like silver is refined, and I will test them like gold is tested. Certainly through torments of fire and punishments, through martyrdoms of faith as a test. The Apostle also knows what kind of God he has ascribed, when he writes: If God did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us, how did He not also give us all things with Him? You see how even His own firstborn and only-begotten Son divine Wisdom slew; certainly, that He might live, and also lead others back into life. I can say with God's Wisdom: Christ is the one who handed Himself over for our sins. Now Wisdom has also slain herself. Words do not sound alone, but also have meaning; nor are they to be heard only with the ears, but also with the minds. The one who does not understand believes in a cruel God. Although even for the one who does not understand, a sentence is set, which checks temerity of understanding otherwise. For who, He says, has known the mind of God? Or who has been His counselor, to instruct Him? Or who has shown Him the way of intelligence? But indeed, it was permitted to placate the Diana of the Scythians, or the Mercury of the Gauls, or the Saturn of the Africans, with human victims in the world. And in Latium, even to this day, human blood is poured out to Jupiter in the middle of the city; nor does anyone retract, or does not presume some reason, or the inestimable will of their god. If our God also had demanded martyrdoms for Himself in the name of His own victim, who would have reproached Him for a funereal religion, and mournful rites, and a funeral pyre for an altar, and a polluting priest? And would not have considered blessed anymore the one whom God had devoured?

pass_b_english: The scorpion still strikes, accusing God of murder. I recoil completely at the filthy state of blasphemy stinking from a heretic's mouth. Yet I will embrace such a God with the confidence of reason, the very reason by which He Himself declared Himself more than a murderer through the person of His Wisdom, speaking in Solomon's voice: 'Wisdom has slain her sons' (Proverbs 8:36). Wisdom is wisdom; she slew wisely, since she sent them into life, and rationally, since she sent them into glory. What genius for parricide! What artistry of crime! What an argument for cruelty: it kills precisely so that the one it kills may not die! So what follows? Wisdom is sung in exits with hymns, for the exits of martyrs are sung too. Wisdom performs constancy in the streets, for she slays her sons well. Trusting in the highest walls, she speaks, for here, according to Isaiah, she cries out: 'I am of God' (Isaiah 44:6); and here she shouts: 'In the name of Jacob'; and another writes: 'In the name of Israel.' What a good mother! I wish to be reduced to her sons, so that she might kill me. I wish to be killed, so that I might become a son. Does she only slay her sons, or does she also torment them? For I hear God saying elsewhere: 'I will refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested.' Certainly through the torments of fire and punishments, through martyrdoms that test faith. The Apostle knows what kind of God he has described, when he writes: 'If God did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how will He not also with Him graciously give us all things?' (Romans 8:32). You see how even His own firstborn and only-begotten Son divine Wisdom slew; surely so that He might live, and bring others back into life. I can say with God's Wisdom: Christ is the one who handed Himself over for our sins. Now Wisdom has slain herself as well. Words do not merely sound; they carry meaning. They are not to be heard only with the ears, but with the mind. The one who does not understand believes in a cruel God. Yet even for the one who does not understand, a sentence stands that restrains the rashness of understanding otherwise. For 'who has known the mind of God? Or who has been His counselor, to instruct Him? Or who has shown Him the way of understanding?' But indeed, it was permitted in the world to appease the Diana of the Scythians, the Mercury of the Gauls, the Saturn of the Africans, with human victims. And in Latium, to this very day, human blood is tasted by Jupiter in the middle of the city; no one retracts it, nor fails to presume some reason for it, or the inestimable will of their god. If our God had also demanded martyrdoms in the name of His own victim, who would have reproached Him for a funereal religion, mournful rites, a funeral pyre for an altar, a polluted priest? And would they not have considered blessed the one whom God had devoured?

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. Scripture citations (Proverbs 8:36, Isaiah 44:6, Romans 8:32) were correctly identified and added to Pass B as required. The title 'God's Wisdom in Martyrdom' accurately reflects the thought of the text. Pass B maintains the agency and nuances of the Latin (e.g., 'Wisdom has slain her sons' and the distinction between 'slaying' and 'tormenting').
